scope: Synthetic HTTP route/session boundary on the current root worktree; not a production-release bar.

candidate.head: eff8e0d8974f2c3222eb4602e4a37ff73c708245
candidate.baseline: AUD-0583 tested a different isolated SHA and is not a baseline for this candidate.

criteria.target: Enumerate Fastify runtime method/path pairs; parse every route-tree line; app.hasRoute confirms every pair.
criteria.validity: Uses the actual built Fastify instance, not source-text route matching.

criteria.target: Every route-method pair except explicit health/observability, idempotent logout, and webhook-signature routes returns HTTP 401 in each no-cookie, forged-header/invalid-token, and unknown-cookie scenario.
criteria.evidence: probe-results.json; route classes are computed from actual registered paths
criteria.validity: Valid Origin avoids conflating CSRF rejection with authentication; an unknown but syntactically valid session ID exercises store lookup failure.

criteria.target: A synthetic live cookie session returns HTTP 200 for GET /v1/session, /v1/tasks and /v1/admin/agents.
criteria.validity: Confirms denial results are not caused by a server that denies all requests.

criteria.target: Record whether a valid synthetic signed token can bootstrap /v1/session, whether replay is rejected, and whether the token authenticates selected protected reads without a cookie; compare observations to SPEC 0144 and existing tests without inventing a policy absent from them.
criteria.evidence: probe-results.json, SPEC 0144, and current API tests
criteria.validity: Separates explicit contract failures from currently ambiguous compatibility behavior.

criteria.target: POST /v1/session/logout without cookie is idempotent, returns HTTP 200, and does not call store.revoke.
criteria.validity: Counts store revocations in the synthetic adapter.

criteria.target: HEAD and the hashed API/shared source manifest remain unchanged from before import through probe completion; exact command outputs and artifact hashes are recorded.
criteria.validity: The probe refuses to produce valid evidence on source drift.

criteria.target: Only synthetic identity, an in-memory store and in-process HTTP injection are used; no PostgreSQL, external IdP/webhook/channel, real data, deploy or production access.
criteria.evidence: probe command, script and runtime profile in probe-results.json
criteria.validity: All requests stay in Fastify inject and test-owned memory adapters.

limitations: This route/authentication audit does not test business correctness of every handler.
Production entrypoint, PostgreSQL session store, corporate OIDC/MFA, webhook signatures and staging are outside this synthetic profile.
A valid HMAC token directly accepted on a protected route is evaluated against the approved session contract and existing compatibility tests; the probe alone cannot create a new policy.
